title: When was creation?
hook: what hour, what season was the world made? only the Creator knows (Japji 21)
tomorrow: what did Guru Nanak see when he looked up at the evening lamps?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the river Bein and the Japji's first stanza: by thinking, He can't be thought, even a hundred thousand times. Beyond thought.

At dinner a kid asks, out of nowhere: but when did the world start? What day? The adults at the table go quiet. Guru Nanak asked the same question. In the Japji's twenty-first stanza: what was that time, what moment, what day, what season, what month, when the world took shape? Then he goes around the room. The pandits didn't find the hour, or it would be written in the Puranas. The qazis didn't find it, or it would be written in the Quran. The yogi doesn't know the day, and nobody knows the season or the month.
screen: `A KID ASKS: WHAT DAY?` → `WHAT HOUR WAS THE WORLD MADE?` → `THE PANDITS, THE QAZIS, THE YOGI.`

segments.voice: Then the answer: the Creator who made the creation, He alone knows. Guru Nanak tells what came before in another hymn of the Guru Granth Sahib, in Raag Maru. For countless ages, he sings, there was only darkness. No earth, no sky. No day, no night, no sun, no moon. Only the hukam, the divine order. Nobody there to keep a calendar. So, in the Japji, the hour of creation belongs to the Creator, and the Japji says so out loud to the learned of every camp around it. It isn't a jab at anyone's books. It's a line drawn around what any book can hold. And it isn't a shrug. The stanza goes on to say that the Creator's greatness can't be described, and that anyone who claims to know it by himself won't be honored in the world to come. Not knowing, in the Japji, is a kind of honesty, and a kind of praise. Worth repeating at dinner: in a single stanza, Nanak names the scholars of the Puranas, the scholars of the Quran and the yogis, and gives none of them the date.
screen: `HE ALONE KNOWS.` · `DARKNESS BEFORE EARTH AND SKY.` · `A LINE AROUND WHAT BOOKS CAN HOLD.` · `NOT KNOWING AS PRAISE.` · then, large: `ONLY THE CREATOR KNOWS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one thing in your life you can't know yet: a result, a reply, an outcome. Don't solve it or rehearse it. Let it sit there, unknown, while the breath comes and goes, and notice that you're still here with it.
When was creation? The Japji's question, and its answer: only the Creator knows.
Hold this one gently: only the creator knows, and the not-knowing can be shared. Two of five from the Japji.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite the Japji each morning; its twenty-first stanza is read as a teaching of humility before what only the Creator, Karta Purakh, knows.

pandits.meaning: learned Hindu scholars of the scriptures

qazis.meaning: Muslim judges and scholars of religious law

Puranas.meaning: Hindu books of old stories about gods and creation

yogi.meaning: here, an ascetic of Guru Nanak's day

Raag Maru.meaning: one of the musical measures of the Guru Granth Sahib
